All these, then, I mean both the animals and the plants, we shall say have the best and the medial mixture within their own genus, not simply when there is an exact equality of the opposites, but when there exists in it the proportion that accords with its capacity. Menecrates did this because it often happens that errors are made in the copying not only by people unwillingly but also by some willingly, out of malice: making the letter O into Θ by drawing another transverse line through the middle of the round line, and the letter iota [into tau] by adding another line, likewise transverse; just as also, when one line is scraped off the letter rho, the shape of iota happens to be left. In the same way, with many letters, by the addition of some strokes, the combination of others and the removal of others, it happens that the characters signifying them are altered. But Menecrates achieved nothing further for the time to come, since those who copied his book wrote the names of the numbers not in full letters but by means of the characters signifying them.
